subject: CardioPay: region binding, transient analytics routing, and DPA addendum
messages:
From: Sara Lynch <sara.lynch@cardiopay.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: region-binding for PHI-like telemetry + transient analytics routing questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CardioPay would like to move forward with a 6-week pilot for payments telemetry. Before we spin up test traffic, legal/security have two gating items:

1) A written commitment that customer data scoped to EU (EU citizens) will be pinned to EU-hosted inference by default (region-binding) and will not be replicated to other regions except under documented, auditable exceptions.
2) Confirmation that aggregated analytics/telemetry processing can be performed outside the EU for a short, transient window (we expect <1 hour) for batch analytics, with logs and proof of deletion after processing. We need to understand the maximum transient window, logging granularity, and whether this processing will touch raw payloads or only derived metrics.

I've attached our screening questionnaire (CardioPay-DPA-questions.pdf) and a short list of required artifacts. Can you confirm Redwood's position and suggest next steps?

Thanks,
Sara Lynch
Head of Security, CardioPay Inc.
Attachments: CardioPay-DPA-questions.pdf

Looping in Kimberly (legal) to confirm the commit language and Laura for implementation/ops to scope the TTL for transient analytics. Marissa will coordinate the pilot contract and schedule.

If you can reply with the exact answers, we will draft an addendum and a short operational playbook.

Markus / team — below is the legal/controls position we can commit to for the pilot and proposed DPA addendum language. Posting it here so CardioPay sees the operational constraints and logging guarantees.

1) Region binding: Redwood will offer an EU tenancy pin for CardioPay. Contractually we will add an addendum stating that customer-scoped inference requests for EU-tagged data are served from EU-hosted nodes by default. The addendum will:
   - Define "EU-tagged data" (customer declaration + routing headers)
   - Require a 48-hour notification window for any planned cross-border processing (non-emergency)
   - Allow emergency/ops fallbacks (multi-region failover) only with documented incident tickets and post-incident audit logs

2) Transient analytics processing: for the pilot we can permit ephemeral analytics outside the EU under these constraints:
   - Maximum transient window: 60 minutes from export time (we recommend 30 minutes; default policy will be set to 60 minutes unless CardioPay requests shorter)
   - Scope: only derived or pseudonymized metrics may be processed outside the EU by default. Export of raw payloads is not permitted without a separate written waiver and strong minimization controls.
   - Auditing: every transient export will create an immutable audit record (timestamp, dataset id, processing node region, job id, and initiating user/service id). Audit logs will be available for 12 months in the Customer Console.
   - Deletion guarantees: processed intermediate payloads on non-EU nodes will be deleted within the transient window and deletion confirmed in the audit trail.

3) Subprocessors and notification: we will provide a roster of subprocessors and a 10-business-day notice period for additions that materially affect data residency. For pilot operations (short-term) we can provide an expedited 5-business-day window if needed and capture it in the addendum.

4) Evidence and artifacts: we will provide SOC 2 type II report excerpts (redacted), a region-routing diagram, and a draft DPA addendum for review.

I'll attach the region routing diagram and a redline-ready addendum. Laura / ops — please confirm that the 60-minute TTL and the audit record fields are supported by the platform.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: region-routing-diagram.png

Sara Lynch
